building.

properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 6 at 5:41PM CDT until August 7 at 12:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Missouri, including the following
counties, Christian, Douglas, Greene, Ozark, Stone, Webster and
Wright.

* WHEN...Until midnight CDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 541 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen with some areas measuring from 1 to 1.5 inches in
as short as 15 minutes.
- This includes the following low water crossings...
Little Beaver Creek at County Road 447, Beaver Creek at
County Road 524, Fox Creek at County Road 246, James River at
Bell Ford Road, Finley River at Johns Ford Road, Bryant Creek
at County Road 223 and Bull Creek at Center Road.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Southern Springfield, Nixa, Ozark, Battlefield, Ava,
Highlandville, Rogersville, Seymour, Sparta, Mansfield,
Fordland, Diggins, Fremont Hills, Duncan, Spokane, Dogwood,
Elkhead, Keltner, Bruner, Goodhope, Oldfield, Chadwick, Rome,
Garrison, Linden, Squires, Christian Center, Turners, Odin,
Selmore, Galloway, Brushyknob, Chestnutridge, Gentryville and
Bryant Creek State Park.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 1:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 12:50pm the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.4 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Wednesday.
-The Yentna River at Lake Creek is forecast to go below flood
stage Saturday morning August 8th.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.




- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
